sub_results.fact: runtime fingerprints (already-obtained; not re-counted as host acceptance)
sub_results.value: python 3.13.0, sqlite 3.45.3, tz +0800 (Asia/Shanghai), AMD64; 5/5 .NET Framework 4 x64 DLL SHA256 match the candidate declaration (System, System.Core, System.ServiceProcess, clr, mscorlib); python.exe SHA256 matches Codex LOCAL_RUNTIME_OBSERVATION

allowed_scope.rules.extensions=[.py]; deny_name_patterns include *.json, *.env*, *.db, *.pem, *.key, *.p12, *.csv; paths whitelist = 13 exact .py files under the production root; max_files_per_release=6; max_patch_bytes=262144
sub_results.note: the candidate payload is config/host.json + runtime/*.json + service/RoktU1Bridge.cs + service/RoktU1Bridge.exe + 2 *.ps1 = 0 of 7 files are .py; the publisher cannot carry any of them

sub_results.value: UNSUPPORTED IN THE APPLY PATH. registry._apply_checks returns {feasible:false, reason:'target_absent'} when the target is not a file, which forces deployable=false; executor.op_apply_multi reads the existing target bytes (line 990) before it can write a backup, so an absent target aborts before any write

sub_results.fact: backup representation when the target does not exist
sub_results.value: THERE IS NO SUCH REPRESENTATION. The literal 'ABSENT' exists only as manifest vocabulary (registry.py:155) and as an attestation branch (registry.py:247-249); the backup step is an unconditional byte copy of an existing file (executor.py:1002-1012) and no absence sentinel is ever written to the backups directory

SUPPORTED: per-file temp file on the same volume, write, fsync, DACL copied from the original, os.replace, then a post-replace SHA+size re-verification for every file; any failure rolls the whole release back

sub_results.fact: deletion rollback (rollback of a file that did not exist before)
sub_results.value: NOT SUPPORTED: op_rollback_multi restores each file from its .before.bak via os.replace and requires current==declared_after and backup==declared_before; there is no branch that deletes a file created by the apply

sub_results.fact: source support vs configuration enablement vs machine acceptance
sub_results.value: source support: atomic replace only. configuration enablement: 4 registered releases, 3 deployable, 0 targeting non-.py paths, and none targeting a not-yet-existing file. machine acceptance for this candidate: NOT PERFORMED (no installation authorised).

items.why_partial: exactly one of the four requested publisher capabilities (atomic replacement) is supported at source level. New-file delivery, backup-or-absence and deletion rollback are architecturally absent. The local Python/.NET fingerprint PASS must NOT be read as publisher or host acceptance.
